title: Sell Mineral Rights in Jefferson, PA
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Jefferson, PA (Greene County)
metaDescription: Jefferson sits in Greene County, arguably the strongest Marcellus and Utica acreage in Pennsylvania. See what that means for your mineral interest.
heroLead: Jefferson sits in Greene County, and if you ask most landmen working Pennsylvania right now, Greene is the county they want acreage in more than any other.
intro: There's a reason Greene County keeps coming up in industry reports as some of the best Marcellus rock in the state, with the Utica sitting even deeper underneath it. Jefferson Township is right in the middle of that. I've talked to families here who signed leases fifteen years ago for numbers that seemed generous at the time, and today their royalty checks reflect wells that are still among the strongest producers CNX and EQT operate anywhere in Pennsylvania.

sections.heading: Why Greene County Rock Runs Deeper and Thicker
paragraphs: Greene sits toward the thermally mature, thicker part of the Marcellus shale window, and it's one of the few counties in the state where operators are also actively developing the deeper Utica formation as a second target from the same pad. That stacked-pay setup is part of why Jefferson-area units tend to draw serious operator interest even in years when drilling slows elsewhere.

sections.heading: Impact Fees Under Act 13
paragraphs: Every unconventional well drilled in Greene County pays an annual impact fee under Act 13, money that flows back to the county and to Jefferson Township itself for roads, infrastructure, and emergency services. It's a separate pot of money from your royalty, but it's a sign of how much drilling activity has actually happened here versus counties where the fee revenue barely registers.

sections.heading: What Makes a Jefferson Interest Worth More or Less
paragraphs: Whether your parcel sits inside a producing unit, a permitted-but-undrilled unit, or open acreage with no unit filed at all changes the picture substantially. We pull that status directly from the county before discussing a range, because a producing Jefferson Township well with strong royalty history supports a very different offer than raw, unleased acreage a few miles away.

faqs.question: Is Greene County really that much better than neighboring counties?
faqs.answer: Industry data has consistently shown Greene among the top-producing Marcellus counties in the state, and the Utica adds a second layer most counties don't have — but every individual parcel still depends on its specific unit and history.

faqs.question: What's an impact fee and do I get any of it?
faqs.answer: Act 13 impact fees are paid by the operator to the county and township, not directly to mineral owners — they're separate from your royalty but a useful signal of drilling activity nearby.

faqs.question: Should I sell now or wait for more wells to be drilled?
faqs.answer: It depends on your risk tolerance and whether a unit is already filed against your acreage — we'll walk through both scenarios honestly rather than pushing you toward selling.
